column4: وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ repeats the section's exact grave-overturning verb, making the raised dust of the opening a rehearsal for opened graves.
People come out of the graves سِرَاعًا and hurry toward a نصب; this is the section's explicit meeting of the running horses with running resurrected humans.
The earth splits from them as they emerge سِرَاعًا, directly joining cracked grave-earth, speed, and the final gathering.
Rain is driven to dead land and brings fruit before كَذَٰلِكَ نُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتَىٰ; it states the section's rain-to-grave analogy outright.
Good soil yields by its Lord's leave whereas foul soil yields only نَكِدًا; this is the productive-earth boundary behind the section's kenūd soil before the same earth opens its graves.
Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend name the accumulated treasure that the section places beside the assaying of what lies in breasts.
Hoarded metal is heated in Hell and used to brand foreheads, sides, and backs, fusing treasure, fire, and the exposure of its owner.
If their wealth were pressed from them they would become miserly and God would bring out أَضْغَانَكُمْ; property and concealed contents are extracted in one statement.
The garden owners swear to cut its crop مُصْبِحِينَ, beginning the exact dawn expedition in which withholding resembles a raid.
A visitation from their Lord circles the garden while they sleep, turning the intended dawn takers into people overtaken before dawn.
By morning the garden is كَالصَّرِيمِ, so the scene's expected harvest has already been cut off by the Lord's answering stroke.
They call one another مُصْبِحِينَ, preserving the section's tightly linked sequence of morning, collective movement, and intended seizure.
Their whispered order that no poor person enter the garden gives the dawn party its clenched-hand purpose.
يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًا depicts people issuing in groups as flocks leave water; it joins the watering-place sense of ṣ-d-r to breasts, emergence, and the sight of deeds.
Humanity answers أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ with بَلَىٰ شَهِدْنَا, the covenant scene behind a human being witness upon himself concerning his Lord.
أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ asks resurrection deniers about the very act of striking forth latent fire developed in the section.
The question whether humans produced the fire's tree or God did makes the hidden flame in wood evidence of divine re-creation.
The challenger asks who will revive bones when they are decayed, supplying the denial to which the section's green-tree fire answers.
The answer that their first Originator will revive them fixes the resurrection claim that the following tree-fire image demonstrates.
God makes fire from the green tree and people kindle from it; latent fire brought out of wood parallels bodies brought out of earth.
The Creator of heavens and earth is declared able to create their like, drawing the tree-fire proof back to bodily resurrection.
The raven shows Cain how يُوَارِي his brother's corpse in earth; the w-r-y wording hides a body where the section's cognate fire-making discloses flame, before graves disclose bodies again.
الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ names the wealth-gatherer whose collection the section sets against the final gathering and sorting.
The wealth-counter of 104:2 is thrown into the Crusher, carrying accumulated property directly into the fire sequence completed in 104:6-7.
نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ supplies the divine fire that answers the wealth-gatherer named in 104:2.
The fire rises over الْأَفْئِدَةِ, joining punishment for amassed wealth to the inward heart exposed in the section.
The blaze لَظَى begins the punishment whose own next clauses call the one who turns away and gathers wealth.
The fire calls whoever أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّى, identifying the human stance that culminates in hoarding in 70:18.
وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ compresses collecting and closing away wealth, exactly the section's gathered treasure and clenched hand.
وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَمًّا portrays all-consuming acquisition, a direct form of the kenūd person's solitary, withholding appetite.
وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا is the Quran's closest explicit restatement of intense love of wealth.
Immediately after the love of wealth, the earth is pounded دَكًّا دَكًّا, joining attachment to property with the final upheaval of ground.
أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ names acquisitive accumulation as the force carrying people toward the grave scene.
حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ places competitive accumulation and graves in the same movement, matching the section's wealth-to-grave turn.
كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ answers heedless accumulation with coming knowledge, as the section asks whether the wealth-lover knows what grave-opening entails.
لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ intensifies the section's movement from unanswered human knowledge to certainty at judgment.
لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ brings the accumulating grave-visitor of 102:1-2 to visible fire.
The grave-visitors are questioned that day about نعيم, turning enjoyed goods into disclosed accountability.
The displayed الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ identifies the excellent horses that the next ayah calls حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ.
Solomon's إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ speaks of the displayed horses with the same love-of-khayr wording that follows the horses in surah 100.
One catalogue of human desire contains hoarded gold and silver and branded horses, bringing the section's opening horses and later wealth-love into a single ayah.
The command to charge with cavalry and infantry then share in الأموال joins an attacking mounted force to corrupted attachment to property.
فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَىٰ brings grain from its enclosure and the living from the dead; ḥabb, the section's lexical heart of ḥubb, is opened into a resurrection image.
Floodwater bears foam while heated ore casts up dross, and what benefits people remains; this is the Quranic assay scene behind separating precious metal from earth and sorting the inward residue.
Within a battle aftermath God tests مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ and assays مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ, directly meeting the outer raid with inward refinement.
God separates the foul from the good, heaps the foul جَمِيعًا, and puts it in Hell; sorting, gathering, and fire converge exactly as in the section's ore image.
يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ makes the judgment day an assay of concealed things, the direct thematic counterpart of sorting what breasts contain.
At the presentation لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ; inward concealment ends when humanity is brought before its Lord.
On the day people are بَارِزُونَ, nothing about them is hidden from God; bodily emergence and total disclosure occur together.
People fold their breasts to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and disclose and is عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ; it states the section's outward-to-inward penetration.
Whether people hide what is in their breasts or reveal it, God knows it, directly answering the section's question about knowledge after breasts are opened.
بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ makes the human being evidence against himself, matching the adverse self-witness reading of 100:7.
Mouths are sealed while hands speak and feet testify to earnings, turning bodily action into testimony against the person who performed it.
Tongues, hands, and feet testify عَلَيْهِمْ about what people did, a direct instance of witness working against its human subject.
At the Fire, hearing, sight, and skins testify against their owners about their deeds, joining embodied witness, exposure, and punishment.
They failed to hide because they assumed God did not know much of what they did; the ayah explicitly connects adverse bodily witness to underestimated divine knowledge.
أُمَّةً وَسَطًا is made so that it may be شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ; “middle” and “witnesses” meet within one ayah as they do across the section's crowd and testimony.
The Last Day is يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ and يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ, fusing universal gathering with witnessed presence.
God raises them all, tells them their forgotten deeds, and is witness over everything; resurrection, inwardly complete reckoning, and witness form one sequence.
The earth's final shaking begins the sequence whose burdens emerge and whose people issue in groups in 99:2 and 99:6.
وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا depicts earth casting out what it carried, the clearest parallel to overturned graves yielding their hidden occupants.
The earth tells its reports, making the previously trodden ground itself a witness when it opens.
The earth reports بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا, locating the opened ground's testimony under the command of the same knowing Lord.
After issuing from the earth, a person sees an atom's weight of خَيْرًا; khayr has become a witnessed deed rather than the property intensely loved in 100:8.
The smallest evil is likewise seen, completing the move from opened earth to exact disclosure of what each person had done.
At Midian's water the women wait حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ الرِّعَاءُ; this actual flock-leaving-water scene supplies the concrete dictionary image carried by يَصْدُرُ in 99:6 and ṣudūr in the section.
Human formation, barren earth, descending water, and stirred growth are staged together as a detailed demonstration addressed to doubters of resurrection.
God will raise مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ, making explicit what the revived-earth demonstration in 22:5 proves.
Winds drive cloud to dead land and revive earth after death, followed by كَذَٰلِكَ النُّشُورُ; rain and emergence are identified.
Humbled earth stirs and swells with rain, and its reviver is declared the reviver of the dead.
Measured water revives a dead land and كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ directly applies that emergence to the hearers.
Rain provision revives dead land and كَذَٰلِكَ الْخُرُوجُ names human coming-out by the same pattern.
A dead earth is revived and حَبًّا is brought out for people to eat; hidden grain, extraction, and life from death meet in one sign.
At the trumpet they move from the graves إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنْسِلُونَ, a rapid human counterpart to the opening charge.
They emerge from graves like scattered locusts, turning hidden bodies into a visible moving multitude.
مُهْطِعِينَ إِلَى الدَّاعِ gives the grave-emergers of 54:7 their urgent directed movement toward the caller.
At one divine call from earth إِذَا أَنْتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ, joining the Lord's summons to sudden bodily emergence.
After a single blast, everyone is suddenly بِالسَّاهِرَةِ on the exposed surface, the endpoint of emergence from below ground.
The earth is laid bare and all people are gathered without one being left, supplying the universal crowd into whose midst the section's movement ends.
Both the former and latter peoples are named before the next ayah gathers them to a fixed time.
لَمَجْمُوعُونَ إِلَىٰ مِيقَاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ states the final universal gathering toward which the image runs.
هَٰذَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ جَمَعْنَاكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ names the assembled crowd as the gathering for decisive separation.
God gathers the messengers, asks what answer they received, and they defer knowledge to the Knower of unseen things; gathering, question, and ultimate knowledge converge.
When the threatened force descends into their courtyard, فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ; the morning assaulters' image is reversed into a terrible morning for those assaulted.
The earth swallows Qarun and his house, so amassed treasure ends with its owner hidden below the same earth that will later cast the buried out.
فَمَا أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ denies that believers spurred horses in this campaign, marking a Quranic boundary to the mounted-raid scene.
Believers are أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ, redirecting the section's intensity of love away from khayr-as-wealth toward God.
Righteousness requires spending مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ, reversing the clenched attachment to beloved property by making that very love the measure of giving.
They prefer others despite their own need and are guarded from the soul's stinginess, the direct ethical opposite of the garden owners' closed hand.
Those who spend for God's pleasure resemble a high garden whose rain doubles its yield, opposing both withheld wealth and foul soil's meagre growth.
People become كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ, a dispersed human swarm that illuminates by reversal the image of entering the middle of a gathered mass.
Their command to go early to the crop continues the purposeful dawn advance begun in 68:17.
They set out whispering, making the morning harvesting party a coordinated secret expedition before 68:24 reveals its aim.
They go early عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ while thinking themselves able, giving the withholding dawn party the hard intent and confidence of an assault.
On seeing the struck garden they think they have lost the way, the first recognition that the intended raiders have themselves been pre-empted.
They recognize that they are deprived, making their planned deprivation of the poor rebound upon them.
كَذَٰلِكَ الْعَذَابُ identifies the ruined garden as divine punishment and points beyond it to the greater afterlife reckoning.
A settled punishment seizes the warned people at morning, another concrete Quranic morning in which the threatened party is overtaken.
Lot is told that his people's appointment is الصُّبْح and asked whether morning is near, tying dawn to an unavoidable divine strike.
The decree that the last of the people will be cut off مُصْبِحِينَ gives morning the same decisive movement from warning to destruction.
The townspeople are asked whether they feel safe from punishment coming بَيَاتًا while asleep, matching the garden owners' nocturnal reversal.
رِبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ is prepared to terrify an enemy, confirming the opening animals as horses readied for hostile action rather than mere travel.
The hand must not be chained to the neck nor wholly outspread; its bodily image sets the boundary around the section's clenched hand of withholding.
The hypocrites يَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ and forget God, giving the closed hand a Quranic moral relation to ingratitude toward the Lord.
What people withhold from God's bounty will be collared around them on resurrection day, converting retained property into exposed judgment.
The one who بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنَىٰ embodies the self-sufficient miserliness developed through the kenūd and garden-owner images.
وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ carries the miser of 92:8 to the point where amassed wealth cannot save him.
The blazing fire warned in this ayah supplies the judgment horizon for the miser and the purifying giver contrasted in the surrounding passage.
The Godfearing person gives his wealth يَتَزَكَّىٰ, reversing hoarding and turning property into a means of inward purification.
Wealth must not distract from God's remembrance; those it distracts are the losers, a direct diagnosis of intense attachment to property.
The command to spend before death arrives makes the closed hand's missed opportunity visible at the boundary of burial and return.
On the final day neither wealth nor children benefit, stripping the loved property of the value assigned to it before judgment.
Only one who comes with a sound heart benefits, setting inward condition against the wealth dismissed in 26:88.
Wealth and children do not avail against God and their owners become fuel for the Fire, another precise wealth-to-fire conjunction.
مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ denies saving power to accumulated property immediately before fire.
The owner whose wealth does not avail in 111:2 enters a blazing fire, completing the property-to-flame movement.
Those who consume orphans' wealth unjustly consume fire into their bellies, making wrongful acquisition already an inward fire.
Qarun's treasure keys burden a strong company, giving amassed wealth the concrete weight that precedes his return into earth.
Qarun claims his treasure came through knowledge he possesses, while the ayah answers with God's prior destruction of stronger accumulators; claimed knowledge meets divine knowledge and judgment.
Worldly rivalry in wealth is compared to rain-grown vegetation that yellows and becomes debris, joining property, soil, and passing yield.
Rain-mingled vegetation becomes dry fragments scattered by wind, a field image in which apparent abundance ends as dispersed matter.
Wealth is the adornment of near life while lasting good deeds are better, interpreting the transient field of 18:45 against attachment to property.
Rain-grown earth reaches full adornment just as its people think they control it, then God's command leaves it harvested; it parallels the garden owners' confident seizure and sudden loss.
A rock bearing dust is stripped bare by downpour as the image of ruined giving, joining dust, rain, and the failure of wealth to yield.
God knows a grain in the darknesses of earth as well as every falling leaf, joining the hidden inner “grain,” buried earth, and exhaustive knowledge.
Whether people disclose or hide what is within themselves, God calls them to account for it, matching the final extraction and divine knowledge of breasts.
أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ asks whether people know that God knows what they conceal and announce, closely matching the section's rhetorical question and hidden interior.
أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا asks whether they know that God knows their secret and private counsel, another exact rhetorical movement from human ignorance to divine knowledge.
Their return is to God, who will tell them what they did and knows what breasts contain; return, disclosed deeds, and inward knowledge are one sequence.
God knows what people conceal and reveal and is عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ, specifying the invisible endpoint of the section's movement inward.
Secret or public speech is alike known by the One who knows what breasts contain, setting a boundary around attempted concealment.
God knows what the self whispers and is nearer than the jugular vein, intensifying the section's final movement into the unseen interior.
The skins answer that God who gives speech to everything made them speak, explaining the adverse testimony staged in 41:20.
The resurrected person reads his own record and is sufficient as accountant against himself, another form of self-testimony at judgment.
The human asks what is happening to the earth, supplying the bewildered human question between its upheaval and its disclosure.
The repeated ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ makes the threatened transition from present heedlessness to final knowledge emphatic.
The Fire is seen عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ, completing the visible certainty promised to the accumulators and grave-visitors.
God brings the living from the dead, the dead from the living, and revives earth, followed by وَكَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ.
The hearer is told to look at revived earth and infer that its reviver gives life to the dead.
Blessed rain produces gardens and grain, beginning the land-revival sequence that 50:11 explicitly calls human emergence.
Tall palms with layered fruit continue the visible yield from rain before the sequence turns to resurrection.
Rain gives dead earth life and is a sign for those who listen, a nonlexical parallel to the grave-soil becoming productive again.
Lightning, hope and fear, rain, and revived earth form another staged sign of life after death.
Provision descending from heaven revives earth after death, repeating the section's field-to-resurrection bridge.
اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا makes revived ground an explicit admonition to know and understand.
Between the barren-earth demonstration and the raised graves, the ayah states that God is the truth and gives life to the dead.
A single rebuking blast precedes humanity's sudden appearance on the surface in 79:14, compressing the opening of the final scene into one sound.
On the day God calls, people answer and think they stayed only a little, a collective movement initiated by the Lord's summons.
The prayer addresses God as the One who gathers all people for a day without doubt, the universal destination implicit in the section's central crowd.
God promises لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ, turning gathering into the Lord's direct, certain act.
The messenger warns of يَوْمَ الْجَمْعِ, naming the eschatological assembly toward which the section's final runners move.
The day God gathers humanity is also the day of mutual loss, adding judgment's separating consequence to the collected crowd.
The earth is convulsed violently at the event, beginning a dust-producing final upheaval continued in 56:5-6.
Mountains are crushed completely, moving the opening scene's raised ground-dust onto a cosmic scale.
The crushed mountains become هَبَاءً مُنْبَثًّا, a final-day cloud of dispersed dust answering the dust raised by hooves.
The earth casts out what is within it and empties, a direct parallel to ground yielding all its buried contents.
After the graves are overturned, each soul knows what it advanced and delayed; exposed earth is followed by exposed moral record.
At the cosmic unveiling every soul knows what it has brought, matching the section's progression from spectacle to inward account.
أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَىٰ uses the same admonishing question to confront a person acting as though divine awareness were absent.
God does not leave the mixed community as it is until He distinguishes the foul from the good, a social counterpart to the section's assay and separation.
وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ may mean that the garden owners made no exception for the poor, directly sharpening their withholding; it may instead refer to failing to say “if God wills.”
وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ can evoke what people inwardly harbor or gather away, but the precise force of يُوعُونَ is broader than the section's chest-assay image.
فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا presents racers whose motion proves precedence, like the opening animal's run witnessing that it has gone ahead; the racers' identity is disputed.

Oil from the blessed tree nearly shines even before fire touches it, a possible Quranic analogue for flame latent in plant matter, though this ayah's governing image is divine light rather than resurrection.
